observations: O1 (fail-closed, cosmetic): staged manifest bytes that are not valid JSON make the gate throw a raw JSON SyntaxError ('Unexpected token...' from JSON.parse inside stagedManifestFromPreview) instead of a controlled refusal message. The apply still rejects and no write happens; the committed case apply_fails_closed_on_non_json_staged_manifest_bytes pins the rejection.

O2 (defense-in-depth note, no write path): the gate reads the first replacement that matches the canonical id or the manifest path. A plan could place clean manifest-shaped bytes on a matching entry and unreviewed delta bytes on a non-matching entry at another canonical destination. No write completes: the exact ordered destination guard forces the four canonical paths in order, and validateCommittedDocument parses each committed document by its replacement id, so the unreviewed bytes fail the baseline schema, the domain check, or the unknown-id check during the transaction. Probing found no combination that reaches a completed write.

O3 (verification of the apply path): applyRepositoryFileTransaction re-derives every destination as resolve(repoRoot, replacement.repositoryPath) and validates repository containment, symbolic links, regular files, realpath canonicalization, and distinct canonical destinations (policy-update-transaction.ts:333-381). The plan's destination and canonicalDestination fields are preview-time facts, not trusted write inputs, so a doctored plan cannot redirect the write.
